History of Quran

تاریخِ قرآن

From the first revelation to the final compiled book — the complete, meticulously preserved journey of the Word of Allah across 23 years of revelation and two great compilations.

23

Years of Revelation

3

Stages of Compilation

Surahs

Huffaz among the Sahabah

Pehli Wahi — پہلی وحی

The First Revelation

The extraordinary night that changed history forever

Before prophethood, Muhammad ﷺ would spend long periods in seclusion (khalwah) in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah, devoting himself to worship and deep reflection, away from the distractions of the world.

Suddenly the angel Jibra’eel (AS) appeared and commanded: "Iqra" (Read!). The Prophet ﷺ replied that he could not read. Jibra’eel embraced him firmly, released him, and repeated the command — three times — until the first words of divine revelation descended.

Place
Jabal al-Noor (Cave of Hira), Makkah al-Mukarramah
Occasion
The month of Ramadan, 610 CE
Age of the Prophet ﷺ
40 years
State
Engaged in seclusion and worship

Makki aur Madani Daur

Makki & Madani Revelation

Two eras, two styles — one divine message across 23 years

The Quran was revealed gradually over 23 years. The Makki period (610–622 CE, 13 years) addressed the polytheists of Makkah with short, powerful, and stirring verses on tawheed, the hereafter, and the stories of the prophets — often beginning with "Ya ayyuhan-nas" (O mankind).

The Madani period (622–632 CE, 10 years) addressed the Muslims and the People of the Book with longer, detailed, legislative verses on law, society, and treaties — often beginning with "Ya ayyuhal-ladhina amanu" (O you who believe).

During the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime the Quran was written down but not yet gathered in one place. More than 40 scribes (Kuttab-e-Wahi) recorded the revelation as it descended.

  • ✦Flat stones (Laukh / Hajarah)
  • ✦Fresh palm branches (Usub al-Nakhl)
  • ✦Bones of camels and horses (Azam)
  • ✦Camel hide (Adeem)
  • ✦Pieces of cloth (Riqaa)
  • ✦Silver tablets (Alwah min Fidda)

Aakhri Wahi

The Final Revelation

The completion of the divine message

According to the well-known position of the scholars, the final verse of the Quran was revealed at Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hujjat ul-Wada’) on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (18 March 632 CE).

The Prophet ﷺ asked the gathering: "Have I conveyed the message? O Allah, bear witness." He passed away only 81 days later, on 12 Rabi ul-Awwal 11 AH. Upon hearing this verse, Umar (RA) wept — sensing that the completion of the religion signalled the approaching departure of the Messenger ﷺ.

During the Prophet’s ﷺ era the Quran was preserved by two mutually confirming methods: memorization (hifz) by over a thousand Companions, and writing (kitabah) by 40+ scribes. Every Ramadan the Prophet ﷺ recited the entire Quran to Jibra’eel — and twice in his final year (Dour-e-Akheer).

Pehla Jamaa' — Abu Bakr (RA) ka Daur

The First Compilation

632–634 CE | The first caliph orders the Quran gathered into one collection

After the Prophet’s ﷺ passing, the false prophet Musaylimah rebelled. At the Battle of Yamama (633 CE) more than 1,200 Muslims were martyred — among them over 70 huffaz. Umar (RA) urged Abu Bakr (RA) to gather the Quran in one place before more of its carriers were lost.

Abu Bakr (RA) initially hesitated: "How can I do something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do?" But Allah opened his heart to it, and he entrusted the task to Zaid ibn Thabit (RA) — the foremost scribe of revelation — who said the task felt heavier than being asked to move a mountain.

Zaid (RA) applied the strictest methodology: he accepted only what was written down with two witnesses AND confirmed by the memory of the huffaz, and only what had been dictated as revelation in the Prophet’s ﷺ presence. The final two verses of Surah At-Tawbah were found in writing only with Khuzaymah al-Ansari (RA), whose testimony the Prophet ﷺ had declared equal to two men.

Result
The Quran gathered for the first time into Suhuf (sheets)
Custody
Kept by Abu Bakr (RA), then Umar (RA), then Umm ul-Mu’mineen Hafsa (RA)
Legacy
These Suhuf later became the foundation of the Uthmani Mushaf

Doosra Jamaa' — Uthman (RA) ka Daur

The Standardization

644–656 CE | 'Jaami' ul-Quran' — one standard Mushaf for the whole Ummah

Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman (RA), campaigning with the armies of Syria and Iraq, saw Muslims disputing over differing recitations — Iraq following Ibn Mas’ood (RA), Syria following Ubayy ibn Ka’b (RA), Madinah following Zaid ibn Thabit (RA). He rushed to Uthman (RA): "O Commander of the Faithful, save this Ummah before they differ over the Book as the Jews and Christians did!"

Uthman (RA) consulted the Companions and, by consensus, formed a committee headed by Zaid ibn Thabit (RA) with Abdullah ibn Zubayr, Sa’eed ibn al-’As, and Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Harith (RA). The Suhuf of Hafsa (RA) served as the foundation; where dialects differed, the Qurayshi form was preferred; only mutawatir (mass-transmitted) readings were accepted; and dots and vowel marks were omitted so the valid readings could all be accommodated.

Five to nine copies were prepared and dispatched with a teacher-reciter to Makkah, Madinah (the Mushaf-e-Imam), Kufa, Basra, and Damascus — and by some reports Bahrain and Yemen. Divergent private copies were destroyed to prevent confusion. The Mushaf-e-Uthmani remains the standard to this day.

Jamaa'-e-Quran ke Aham Sahaba

The Key Companions

The blessed personalities behind the preservation

Zaid ibn Thabit (RA) is the central figure: chosen as a scribe of revelation at just 17, present at the Prophet’s ﷺ final review of the Quran, leader of both compilations, and instructed by the Prophet ﷺ to learn the Torah’s script and Syriac.

  • ✦Zaid ibn Thabit (RA) — scribe of revelation, led both the first and second compilations
  • ✦Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) — gave the first command to gather the Quran
  • ✦Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) — first proposed the compilation and safeguarded the Suhuf
  • ✦Uthman ibn Affan (RA) — "Jaami’ ul-Quran", standardized the Mushaf for the whole world
  • ✦Hafsa bint Umar (RA) — trusted custodian of the Suhuf between the two compilations
  • ✦Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) — scribe of revelation who upheld the Uthmani Mushaf in his caliphate

Ilm-e-Qira'at

The Science of Qira’at

Seven ahruf, ten canonical readings — all traced to the Prophet ﷺ

The Quran was revealed upon seven ahruf (modes), from which the famous canonical Qira’at emerged — each with an unbroken chain of transmission to the Prophet ﷺ: Nafi’ (Madinah), Ibn Katheer (Makkah), Abu Amr (Basra), Ibn Aamir (Sham), Asim (Kufa), Hamza (Kufa), and Kisai (Kufa).

Today the riwayah of Hafs ’an Asim is the most widespread in the world, while Warsh ’an Nafi’ is recited across North and West Africa.

Hifazat-e-Quran — Allah ka Wada

The Divine Promise of Preservation

A promise being fulfilled for over 1,400 years

The Quran is the only book in history preserved letter-for-letter for over fourteen centuries. More than ten million huffaz across the world carry it in their hearts; children still memorize it completely by the age of seven to nine; and every Ramadan it is recited in full in Taraweeh across the globe. Every hafiz’s chain of transmission (isnad) reaches back to the Prophet ﷺ himself.

The Complete Timeline

From the first revelation to the Mushaf-e-Uthmani

  1. 610 CE

    The First Revelation

    The first 5 verses of Surah Al-Alaq revealed in the Cave of Hira

  2. 610–622 CE

    The Makki Period

    13 years — revelation of tawheed, the hereafter, and the stories of the prophets

  3. 622 CE

    Hijrah to Madinah

    The Prophet ﷺ migrates — the Madani period begins

  4. 622–632 CE

    The Madani Period

    10 years — revelation of law, governance, and treaties

  5. 632 CE

    Hujjat ul-Wada'

    The final revelation — Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3 at Arafah

  6. 632 CE

    Passing of the Prophet ﷺ

    12 Rabi ul-Awwal — the Quran preserved in both memory and writing

  7. 633 CE

    Battle of Yamama

    70+ huffaz martyred — the need for compilation becomes urgent

  8. 633 CE

    The First Compilation

    Abu Bakr (RA) commissions Zaid ibn Thabit (RA) to prepare the Suhuf

  9. 634 CE

    Suhuf passes to Umar (RA)

    Safeguarded after the passing of Abu Bakr (RA)

  10. 644 CE

    Suhuf passes to Hafsa (RA)

    Entrusted to the Mother of the Believers after Umar (RA)

  11. 644–656 CE

    The Second Compilation

    Uthman (RA) commissions the standard Mushaf

  12. ~650 CE

    The Mushaf-e-Uthmani

    Copies sent across the Islamic world — standardization complete

وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ

SubhanAllah — this Quran is the Word of Allah, and its preservation is His promise.
